description: Transport your taste buds to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast with this authentic Focaccia Genovese. Featuring a gloriously crispy crust, an incredibly soft and airy interior, and the aromatic embrace of fresh rosemary and rich olive oil, this traditional bread is a true Italian masterpiece. Perfect as an appetizer, side, or a delightful snack on its own, it embodies the simple elegance of Italian baking.

ingredients.notes: plus extra for drizzling and pan prep

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Stir gently and let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active. This step is crucial for a light and airy focaccia.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Gradually add 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, incorporating it fully. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough will be quite sticky at first.

instructions.title: First Rise (Bulk Fermentation)
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the kneaded dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size. This slow rise develops flavor.

instructions.title: Shape the Focaccia
instructions.text: Generously grease a 9x13 inch baking pan with olive oil. Gently transfer the risen dough to the pan. Using your fingertips, gently stretch and press the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. If the dough resists, let it rest for 10 minutes and try again. Create characteristic dimples all over the surface with your fingers.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Topping
instructions.text: Drizzle the top of the dough generously with more olive oil. Sprinkle the chopped fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt evenly over the surface. Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap and let it rise again in a warm spot for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. Preheat your oven to 220C (425F) during the last 15 minutes of this rise.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and cooked through. The crust should be crispy and the interior soft. Keep an eye on it to prevent over-browning.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven. Immediately drizzle a final touch of extra virgin olive oil over the hot focaccia for extra flavor and shine. Let it cool in the pan for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Slice and serve warm or at room temperature. Buon appetito!

tips: Do not skimp on the olive oil. It is fundamental to the authentic flavor and texture of Focaccia Genovese, both in the dough and as a generous topping.
For the best texture, ensure your water temperature for yeast activation is just right. Too hot will kill the yeast, too cold will not activate it properly. Aim for lukewarm.
If you want an even crispier bottom crust, place a baking steel or pizza stone in your oven while preheating and bake the focaccia directly on it (still in its pan).
article:
Focaccia Genovese, a culinary masterpiece hailing from the Ligurian coast of Italy, is more than just bread; it's an experience. Imagine a golden-crusted, impossibly airy flatbread, generously adorned with fragrant rosemary and glistening with the finest extra virgin olive oil. This authentic Focaccia Genovese, distinct from its thicker relatives, boasts a thin, crisp bottom, incredibly soft interior, and signature dimples that hold pools of savory olive oil and coarse sea salt. It's a testament to simple, high-quality ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating that authentic Italian bakery experience in your own kitchen, you’ve come to the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through the secrets of mastering the perfect Focaccia Genovese, including a detailed Focaccia Genovese recipe. Prepare to embark on a delicious journey into the heart of Italian baking.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?
Focaccia Genovese, or "Fügassa" in the local Ligurian dialect, is a flat oven-baked Italian bread originating in Genoa, the capital of Liguria. It’s distinguished by its thinner profile compared to other focaccia variations, boasting a delightfully crisp bottom crust and an incredibly open, airy crumb with large, irregular holes, often described as "alveolated." This unique texture is achieved through a high hydration dough and specific proofing techniques.

What truly sets Focaccia Genovese apart is its dedication to olive oil. Extra virgin olive oil is paramount, generously incorporated into the dough, used to oil the baking pan, and drizzled over the surface, creating that signature crispness and rich flavor. The deep dimples pressed into the dough aren't merely decorative; they serve a crucial purpose: to trap the olive oil and coarse sea salt, ensuring every bite is a burst of savory flavor. Fresh rosemary adds the classic aromatic touch, its piney aroma perfectly complementing the richness of the olive oil and the subtle sweetness of the bread.

## Ingredients for Authentic Focaccia Genovese
Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese requires a careful selection of a few, high-quality ingredients. To truly master the Focaccia Genovese recipe, understanding each component is key.

*   **Strong Bread Flour (Type 0 or 00):** A high-protein flour (around 12-14%) is crucial for developing strong gluten, essential for trapping gases and creating those large, airy pockets.
*   **Water:** Lukewarm water is needed to activate the yeast. A high hydration dough (often 70-80% of the flour weight) is key for an open crumb.
*   **Fresh Yeast or Active Dry Yeast:** Ensure it’s fresh and active. Fresh yeast offers a subtle flavor, but active dry works well.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** Incorporated into the dough for flavor and to help control fermentation.
*   **A Pinch of Sugar (Optional):** A small amount can help kickstart yeast activity, especially with active dry yeast.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil (EVOO):** This cannot be stressed enough. Use a good quality, fruity, robust extra virgin olive oil. It’s integral to the dough, pan-oiling, and topping.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Sprigs of fresh rosemary provide the signature aromatic touch. Fresh is vastly superior to dried.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt (Maldon or flaky sea salt):** Sprinkled generously over the top before baking, it provides bursts of salty crunch.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Baking Focaccia Genovese
Embarking on this Focaccia Genovese recipe is a rewarding journey, but patience is essential, as the dough requires ample time to develop flavor and texture.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water, a pinch of sugar (if using), and your yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Begin mixing with a sturdy spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Drizzle in 2-3 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil and continue mixing until the oil is absorbed. The dough will be very sticky – resist the urge to add more flour.
3.  **Knead (or Stretch and Fold):** For about 5-7 minutes, knead the dough on a lightly oiled surface until it becomes smoother and more elastic. Alternatively, perform a series of "stretch and folds" in the bowl: every 20-30 minutes for 2 hours, gently stretch a portion of the dough up and fold it over itself.
4.  **First Proof:** Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover tightly with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size. For deeper flavor, a cold proof in the refrigerator for 8-24 hours is highly recommended.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally oil a 9x13 inch (or similar sized) baking pan with a generous amount of extra virgin olive oil. This oil contributes significantly to the crispy bottom.
6.  **Transfer and Dimple:** Gently turn the dough out into the prepared pan. Using oiled fingertips, gently spread the dough to the edges of the pan. This might take a few minutes as the dough relaxes. Once spread, deeply dimple the entire surface of the dough with your fingertips, pressing all the way down to the bottom of the pan.
7.  **Second Proof:** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap and let the dough rise again for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
8.  **Final Touches & Bake:** Preheat your oven to a high temperature, typically 425-450°F (220-230°C). Just before baking, drizzle another generous amount of extra virgin olive oil over the dimpled surface. Scatter fresh rosemary sprigs and coarse sea salt evenly over the top.
9.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-30 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and the bottom is crisp and golden.
10. **Cool:** Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia from the pan to a wire rack to cool slightly. This prevents the bottom from becoming soggy. Slice and serve warm. This Focaccia Genovese recipe is truly a keeper!

## Tips for the Best Focaccia Genovese
Achieving focaccia perfection involves a few key considerations:

*   **Quality Olive Oil is Non-Negotiable:** A robust, flavorful extra virgin olive oil will elevate your focaccia from good to outstanding.
*   **High Hydration Dough:** Don't be afraid of a sticky dough. A high water content is what gives Focaccia Genovese its characteristic airy, open crumb. Resist the urge to add too much extra flour during kneading.
*   **Long Proofing for Flavor:** While a shorter proof works, allowing the dough to rise slowly, especially with a cold proof in the refrigerator overnight, develops a much deeper, more complex flavor profile.
*   **Generous Dimpling:** Those signature dimples aren't just for looks. They create crucial pockets for the olive oil and salt, ensuring every bite is flavorful and moist. Press firmly!
*   **Don't Skimp on Toppings:** Be liberal with the final drizzle of olive oil, fresh rosemary, and coarse sea salt. These elements are not mere garnishes; they are integral to the Genovese experience.
*   **Hot Oven:** A high oven temperature ensures a quick rise and a crispy crust. If you have a pizza stone, preheating your pan on it can further enhance the crispy bottom.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings
Focaccia Genovese is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in countless ways:

*   **Simply Plain:** The traditional Genovese way is to enjoy it plain, perhaps with a morning coffee or as an afternoon snack.
*   **Dipping:** Serve alongside a small dish of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping.
*   **Antipasto Platter:** It's a natural fit for an Italian antipasto spread, complementing cured meats, cheeses, and marinated vegetables beautifully.
*   **Sandwiches:** Its airy texture makes it an excellent choice for sandwiches. Fill it with prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, tomatoes, and basil.
*   **Accompaniment:** Serve it as a side to soups, salads, or pasta dishes, using it to sop up delicious sauces.
*   **Wine Pairings:** Pair with light-bodied Italian reds like Dolcetto or Vermentino for white wine lovers.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic rosemary and olive oil Focaccia Genovese is perfect, feel free to experiment:

*   **Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional, you can try fresh thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs.
*   **Toppings:** Before the final proof, you can press in cherry tomatoes (halved), thinly sliced red onion, black olives, or even a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese.
